title: Age of the Debt and the Lump-Sum Settlement Percent, Deficiency Balance Accounts
content:
**Rule.** The lump-sum debt age of an account held under Deficiency Balance Accounts is the number of whole months from its opening date to today. A lump-sum debt age below 9 whole months adds 5.0 percentage points to the lump-sum settlement percent, one of at least 9 but below 18 whole months adds 2.5 points, and an older debt adds no points. Whole months are counted as the difference in calendar months between the two dates, less one when the later date's day of the month is below the earlier date's.

## Ladder

| Lump-sum debt age | Points added |
|---|---|
| 0 to 8 whole months | 5.0 |
| 9 to 17 whole months | 2.5 |
| 18 whole months or more | None |

## Boundary pairs (hypothetical; account opened on the 10th of a month)

| Today | Whole months | Points added |
|---|---|---|
| The 9th, nine months after opening | 8 | 5.0 |
| The 10th, nine months after opening | 9 | 2.5 |
| The 9th, eighteen months after opening | 17 | 2.5 |
| The 10th, eighteen months after opening | 18 | None |

The opening date is the sale date on which the account opened; payments, credits and arrangements since then do not change the debt age.
